project.title: The Meme Ontology
project.description: MEMO: an OWL ontology of internet memes, built from scraped meme data, linked to Wikidata and queryable with SPARQL.
project.introText: MEMO is an ontology of internet memes, from my master's research Towards an Ontology of Memes (supervisor Fabio Vitali), which I began as a research intern at the Institute of Network Cultures in Amsterdam.

gridImages.caption: Temporal distribution of memes by format.
Variant gallery: the dimensions along which a meme is transformed.

project.middleText: Following Lev Manovich's cultural analytics, it treats memes as a large dataset rather than isolated texts. Around 5,000 images and their metadata, scraped from Know Your Meme, are described in an OWL ontology informed by FRBR across three areas: visual content, cultural references and format. CLIP is used to classify them semi-automatically.
project.conclusionText: The ontology is published with LODE documentation, interactive visualisations of formats, platforms, periods and variants, and a SPARQL explorer with example queries, including links to Wikidata for regions and platforms.
